frames.narration: A page is being built and needs Alice's newest friends. The web server calls the TAO API with a range query: the friend associations from Alice, newest first, limit 10. It never decides which cache or database to use.

The request goes to a follower cache, which is the tier clients talk to. The shard of Alice's id decides which follower holds her association lists. The follower does not have this list yet, so it has a miss.
On a miss a follower asks the leader of the shard. The leader does not have it either, and it is the only tier that is allowed to read the regional MySQL, so it reads the list from there.

The list comes back through the leader and the follower, and each keeps a copy on the way. The next range query for Alice's friends is answered by the follower from memory, with no hop to the leader or the database. This is the normal case.
Now Alice adds Dave as a friend. The write goes from the follower to the leader and to MySQL. TAO also creates the inverse edge, from Dave to Alice, in the same operation.
The reply to the successful write travels back along the same path, and the leader and the follower update their cached lists as it passes. Alice reloads and sees Dave in her list at once.

Another region keeps a copy of the shard. MySQL replication sends the update there, so readers in that region see Dave a little later: eventual consistency is the default. A write made in that region is forwarded to the primary region first.
